First, we select the identity that contains a ${tan}^{2}⁡x$ term. We can use the identity 

$$
1+{tan}^{2}⁡x={sec}^{2}⁡x.
$$

Using the above, we compute the given integral as follows:

$$
\begin{aligned}{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}\frac{9-9{tan}^{4}⁡x}{1-{tan}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x & =9{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}\frac{1-{tan}^{4}⁡x}{1-{tan}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =9{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}\frac{(1-{tan}^{2}⁡x)(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x)}{1-{tan}^{2}⁡x}\,\text{d}x \\  & =9{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}(1+{tan}^{2}⁡x)\text{d}x \\  & =9{\int }_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6}{sec}^{2}⁡x\,\text{d}x \\  & =9\operatorname{tan}⁡x\,{|}_{-\pi /6}^{\pi /6} \\  & =9\operatorname{tan}⁡(\frac{\pi }{6})-9\operatorname{tan}⁡(-\frac{\pi }{6}) \\  & =9\cdot \frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}-9(-\frac{\sqrt{3}}{3}) \\  & =3\sqrt{3}+3\sqrt{3} \\  & =6\sqrt{3}\end{aligned}
$$
